messages:
Eli M: ran a few nsys perf traces on the kvcache + batching path, and the perfetto timeline looks weird — big NVTX blocks that swallow many small kernel launches. attaching the nsys cmd I used: `nsys profile --sample=none -o run1 --trace=cuda,osrt ./run_infer.sh`

Sana R: that usually means our NVTX ranges are too coarse or we push at request-level only. do we have per-kernel ranges?

Devin K: we only push a `NVTX_PUSH(\"request\")` at the start and pop at end for most codepaths. kernels get no explicit ranges — kernels appear inside the request range and look like one big chunk in perfetto.

Eli M: exact. It makes hotspot identification hard because perfetto collapses everything under the outer range. we need finer spans: batching loop, kernel selection, queue wait, kvcache lookup, kvcache writeback, and per-kernel nvtx ranges.

Perf Bot: quick nsys summary (run1): top cuda time -> conv_gemm_launcher (42%), randomize_rng (9%), cross_attention_kernel (18%), host sync ops (12%). note: host sync spikes map to `request` NVTX span.

Marta G: suggestion: adopt a naming convention that includes both request id (short hash) and span role. e.g. `req=abcd12 stage=batch select=kernelA` or `rid:abcd12 | batched_kv_lookup` so we can filter across perfetto by stage.

Devin K: I like `rid=<short> tag=<stage> meta=<hint>` pattern. shorter is better for UI. maybe `r=abcd12 s=batch k=kv_lookup`. also we should only attach `r=` to spans that are per-request; global spans (like worker-thread main loop) omit rid to reduce noise.

Eli M: agree. also propose kernel-level ranges be `k=<kernel_name> cfg=<seq,bs,quant>` so timeline shows kernel identity + config. example: `r=abcd12 s=kernel k=attn cfg=128x8q`.

Sana R: watch overhead. NVTX push/pop per small op could add cost. we should gate fine-grained spans behind a runtime flag or env `RW_NVTX_DETAILED=1`. with default we keep request-level + batching boundaries.

Devin K: got it. implementation plan:
- add optional detailed NVTX instrumentation behind flag
- push `r=<hash>` at request entry (existing)
- push `s=batch` at batching loop entry, `s=select` around kernel selection logic, `s=kv_get` and `s=kv_set` in kvcache paths
- wrap individual kernel launch calls with `k=<kernel> cfg=...` spans when flag enabled

Eli M: plus small changes to kernel selection telemetry: when selecting quantized kernels, append `sel=q8` or `sel=f16` to NVTX string so perfetto filters show different kernel choices. That helps correlate slow traces with bad kernel picks.

Marta G: on naming length — nvtx range names get truncated in perfetto UI. favour concise keys with equals and commas, like `r=abcd,s=batch,k=attn,c=128x8q`.

Perf Bot: FYI, I ran a quick smoke with per-kernel NVTX enabled on dev box (RW_NVTX_DETAILED=1). The overhead measured ~0.7% added per-request at bs=1, negligible at bs>=8.

Sana R: good. two other considerations:
- ensure balanced push/pop even on early returns/exceptions (use RAII guard)
- provide helper that formats the short req hash from 64-bit trace id for readability

Devin K: will implement RAII guard in C++ runtime; add helper in Python shim too. putting it behind flag simplifies rolling back.

Eli M: one more: batch flush paths currently call kernels from different threads. we should include `thread=<id>` or `worker=<pool>` in spans when cross-thread to avoid grouping unrelated ops. maybe only add `w=1` not full thread name.

Marta G: for perfetto queries we'll document a few common filters: `textSearch: \"s=select\"` and `textSearch: \"k=attn\"`, also `regex: r=[0-9a-f]{6}` to group by request fingerprint. I'll add to eng-runtime wiki. :memo:

Devin K: action items:
- (DEVIN) PR to add gated NVTX spans for select/kv/cache/kernel by EOD Thu
- (ELI) run broad perf sweep with gated spans on a few workloads and post nsys + perfetto links
- (MARTA) write short naming convention doc and example perfetto filters
- (SANA) review for privacy/security (ensure no PII in spans)

Eli M: noted. will avoid full UUIDs in NVTX strings, only short hashes. starting work now, will post initial diff.

Perf Bot: automated job queued: `nsys batch-trace --label=nvtx-smoke --env=RW_NVTX_DETAILED=1` — will upload results to the traces bucket when done. :rocket:
